items.name: animate
items.title: Animate
items.description: Wrap anything (logo, screenshot, card, image) to give it a themed enter and exit. The swiss-army knife of reelcn.
items.docs: Usage:

use: Entrances and exits for logos, screenshots, cards and anything without its own animation
Quick prototypes before reaching for a dedicated component
avoid: Headlines — use `text-reveal`

items.name: app-promo
items.title: App Promo
items.description: Vertical app ad: the app's name and promise, its screens on a phone or laptop, its rating, and a download call.

use: App store previews and paid social ads
Showing a mobile or desktop app screen by screen
avoid: A web product in a browser window — use `product-launch`

items.name: app-window
items.title: App Window
items.description: Native desktop window with a title bar and no address bar, wrapped around any app content you pass as children.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <AppWindow title="Settings">
    <div style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%", background: "#fff" }} />
  </AppWindow>
</Center>

use: Framing a desktop app, editor or settings panel in a launch video
Two app windows side by side inside `split-screen`
avoid: A website with an address bar — use `browser-window`

items.name: area-chart
items.title: Area Chart
items.description: Line chart with a gradient fill that is revealed by a clip following each line as it draws.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <AreaChart
    labels={["Mon", "Tue", "Wed", "Thu", "Fri", "Sat", "Sun"]}
    series={[{ label: "Visitors", points: [3200, 4100, 3900, 5200, 6100, 4800, 7400] }]}
  />
</Center>

use: Volume over time: traffic, storage used, cumulative revenue
One or two series where the filled shape carries the story
avoid: Three or more overlapping series — use `line-chart`

items.name: arrow
items.title: Arrow
items.description: Hand-drawn arrow that draws itself from one point to another along a gentle curve, then flicks its head on.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Arrow from={{ x: 27, y: 72 }} to={{ x: 47, y: 48.5 }} label="Best week yet" />

use: Pointing at a detail in a screenshot, chart or product demo
Annotating a feature with a short handwritten-style label
avoid: Circling a whole card or number — use `scribble-circle`

items.name: audio-reactive
items.title: Audio Reactive
items.description: Wraps anything and drives its scale, or a glow, from how loud the audio is right now.
items.docs: Usage:

use: Making a logo, headline or card move with the track
Reacting to a voice whose tempo you do not know
avoid: A known BPM, where pure math is steadier — use `use-beat`

items.name: audiogram
items.title: Audiogram
items.description: Square podcast clip with cover art, show and episode titles, a live waveform of the audio, speaker names and captions.

use: Sharing a podcast episode or segment on social feeds
Turning any voice recording into a video
avoid: A short vertical teaser built on one quote — use `podcast-teaser`

items.name: aurora
items.title: Aurora
items.description: Translucent curtains of accent and highlight light that sway slowly across the top of the frame.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <Aurora />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Atmospheric openers, reveals and calm title scenes
Night-sky, wellness or premium product moods
avoid: Flat, evenly lit color — use `gradient-mesh`

items.name: bar-chart
items.title: Bar Chart
items.description: Bars that grow in one by one over nice gridlines with counting value labels; vertical in landscape and square, horizontal in portrait.

use: Comparing a handful of categories: revenue by quarter, survey answers, signups by channel
Calling out one bar in the accent while the rest stay muted
avoid: Rankings that change over time — use `bar-race`
Trends across many points — use `line-chart`

items.name: bar-race
items.title: Bar Race
items.description: Ranked horizontal bars that grow and swap places smoothly as values change step by step, with a large step label.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence durationInFrames={150}>
  <Center>
    <BarRace
      steps={["2021", "2022", "2023", "2024"]}
      series={[
        { label: "Atlas", values: [12, 30, 45, 61] },
        { label: "Nimbus", values: [25, 34, 40, 44] },
        { label: "Quill", values: [8, 20, 52, 70] },
      ]}
    />
  </Center>
</Sequence>

use: Rankings over time: adoption by year, votes by round, leaderboard changes
Five to twelve series with a value at every step
avoid: A single snapshot — use `bar-chart`

items.name: beams
items.title: Beams
items.description: Soft shafts of accent light fanning out from a corner and sweeping slowly, like stage lights through haze.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <Beams origin="top-left" />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Launch reveals, award-style titles and event promos
Adding energy behind a logo or headline without busy shapes
avoid: A single soft pool of light — use `spotlight`

items.name: before-after
items.title: Before After
items.description: Comparison slider: a divider with a handle wipes from one position to another, revealing "after" past it.
items.docs:
Usage:

<BeforeAfter labels={["Before", "After"]} before={<OldUI />} after={<NewUI />} />

use: Redesigns, edits and upgrades — anything with a clear before and after state
A single screenshot that changes at one point, rather than two panes shown at once
avoid: Two panes shown side by side the whole time — use `split-screen`

items.name: bento-grid
items.title: Bento Grid
items.description: Grid of themed feature tiles that reveal one after another and reflow to four, three or two columns by orientation.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <BentoGrid
    tiles={[
      { title: "Themes", body: "Six presets, one prop", span: 2, accent: true },
      { title: "Responsive", body: "16:9, 9:16 and 1:1" },
      { title: "Deterministic", body: "Seeded, frame-driven" },
    ]}
  />
</Center>

use: Product feature overviews, launch recaps and "what's new" slides
Summing up four to eight short points on one screen
avoid: Cards in a single row or column, use `stagger`

items.name: blur-in
items.title: Blur In
items.description: Headline whose words fade up out of a soft blur, one after another.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <BlurIn text="Quietly, then all at once" />
</Center>

use: Calm, premium intros and brand statements
Titles laid over footage or gradients
avoid: Punchy, high-energy hooks — use `pop-in`

items.name: bokeh
items.title: Bokeh
items.description: Seeded out-of-focus light discs floating upward, larger and softer ones moving faster for depth.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <Bokeh />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Warm, celebratory or lifestyle scenes: holidays, thank-yous, testimonials
A soft, cinematic backdrop behind quotes and names
avoid: Tiny pin-sharp points of light — use `starfield`

items.name: brand-solid
items.title: Brand Solid
items.description: Theme background with a slow, breathing radial tint of the accent color for clean brand scenes.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <BrandSolid />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Title cards, logo reveals and end screens that need a calm, on-brand canvas
Text-heavy scenes where a busier background would compete with the words
avoid: Scenes that need visible movement behind them — use `gradient-mesh`

items.name: brand-sweep
items.title: Brand Sweep
items.description: Layered panels in the brand colors sweep diagonally across the frame, cover the cut, then peel away in reverse order onto the next scene.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={90}>
    <Chapter1 />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={brandSweep()} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 30 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={90}>
    <Chapter2 />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Branded section breaks in explainers and launch videos
Moving between topics with the brand palette on screen

items.name: browser-window
items.title: Browser Window
items.description: Neutral browser chrome with back/forward arrows and a rounded url pill, wrapped around any page content you pass as children.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <BrowserWindow url="reelcn.dev/pricing">
    <div style={{ width: "100%", height: "100%", background: "#fff" }} />
  </BrowserWindow>
</Center>

use: Framing a website, landing page or web app screenshot in a launch or demo video
Two pages side by side inside `split-screen` for a before/after
avoid: A native desktop app with a title bar and no address bar — use `app-window`

items.name: button
items.title: Button
items.description: Primary or secondary button that steps through idle, hover, press, loading and success — the loading spinner and success check crossfade in place, so the button never resizes.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Button
    id="pay-button"
    label="Pay $48.20"
    steps={[{ at: 0, state: "idle" }, { at: 1, state: "press" }, { at: 1.4, state: "loading" }, { at: 2.4, state: "success" }]}
  />
</Center>

use: A UI-sim walkthrough where a cursor clicks a real, named button
A `ui` scene's `component: "button"`
avoid: A static call-to-action with no interaction — use plain text instead

items.name: callout
items.title: Callout
items.description: Dims the frame around a target rectangle, rings it, and points a label bubble at it from the side with the most room.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence from={30} durationInFrames={90}>
  <Callout target={{ x: 65, y: 71, width: 23, height: 8 }} label="Ship it from here" />
</Sequence>

use: Highlighting a button, field or panel in product demos and walkthroughs
Explaining one region of a screenshot or screen recording
avoid: A quick pointer that leaves the rest of the frame undimmed — use `arrow`

items.name: camera
items.title: Camera
items.description: Virtual camera that pans, zooms, rolls and shakes over whatever it wraps, eased between keyframes.
items.docs: Usage:

use: Pushing in on a detail of a screenshot, dashboard or illustration, then pulling back out
Handheld energy or an impact shake on a title card
Splitting a scene into background/foreground layers that parallax at different strengths
avoid: Giving one element its own zoom or slide entrance, use `animate`

items.name: captions-bold-pop
items.title: Captions: Bold Pop
items.description: Heavy centered captions where the spoken word grows and lifts.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsBoldPop captions={captions} emphasize={["free"]} />

use: Shorts and reels that need captions to carry the edit

items.name: captions-boxed
items.title: Captions: Boxed
items.description: Each word in its own rounded chip, with the spoken chip filled in the accent color.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsBoxed captions={captions} />

use: Busy footage where plain text would get lost

items.name: captions-highlight-box
items.title: Captions: Highlight Box
items.description: A marker block travels word by word, like a highlighter following the speech.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsHighlightBox captions={captions} emphasize={["never"]} />

use: Explainers and teaching clips where the key word should be unmissable

items.name: captions-karaoke
items.title: Captions: Karaoke
items.description: Captions that fill in word by word as they are spoken, and dim the words still to come.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsKaraoke captions={captions} />

use: Lyric videos and sing-along clips
Tutorials where viewers follow along word by word

items.name: captions-minimal
items.title: Captions: Minimal
items.description: Quiet captions: one line, no effects, with only the spoken word brightening.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsMinimal captions={captions} />

use: Interviews and documentary footage where captions should stay out of the way

items.name: captions-neon
items.title: Captions: Neon
items.description: Captions where the spoken word glows in the accent color.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsNeon captions={captions} />

use: Night-time and club footage, music clips
avoid: Corporate or documentary footage — use `captions-minimal`

items.name: captions-subtitle-bar
items.title: Captions: Subtitle Bar
items.description: Broadcast-style subtitles on a translucent bar, readable over anything.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsSubtitleBar captions={captions} position="bottom" />

use: Long-form video, webinars and anything with a wide audience

items.name: captions-word-stack
items.title: Captions: Word Stack
items.description: Words stacked one per line, with the spoken word growing and lifting.
items.docs:
Usage:

<CaptionsWordStack captions={captions} maxWords={3} />

use: Vertical video where a wide caption block would crowd the frame

items.name: captions
items.title: Captions
items.description: Word-synced captions that page like TikTok, highlight the spoken word and pop the words you choose.

use: Shorts, reels and talking-head videos that need burned-in captions
Podcast and tutorial clips watched without sound
avoid: A single static line of text — use `text-reveal`

items.name: card-push
items.title: Card Push
items.description: The outgoing scene shrinks into a rounded card and flies off while the next scene rises from behind as a card and expands to full frame.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={90}>
    <FeatureOne />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={cardPush({ direction: "left" })} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 30 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={90}>
    <FeatureTwo />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Stepping through screens, slides or features like a deck of cards
Product walkthroughs and app demos

items.name: changelog
items.title: Changelog
items.description: Release video listing what is new, improved and fixed in a version, three changes per card set.

use: Monthly or per-release update videos
Turning a changelog page into something people watch
avoid: A whole product story — use `product-launch`

items.name: chapter-title
items.title: Chapter Title
items.description: A numbered chapter card that wipes in over the footage and leaves again.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence from={300} durationInFrames={110}>
  <ChapterTitle number={2} title="Setting the key light" />
</Sequence>

use: Section breaks in tutorials and long-form video
Naming the step a viewer is about to watch
avoid: A speaker's name — use `lower-third`

items.name: char-rise
items.title: Char Rise
items.description: A short word or name whose characters rise in one after another.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <CharRise text="Launch day" size={150} />
</Center>

use: Single words, names and short brand lines
Big title cards with only a few letters
avoid: Sentences longer than a few words — use `rise-up`

items.name: chart-scale
items.title: Chart Scale
items.description: Pure math shared by the data components: nice axis ticks, linear scales, an on-theme series palette and jitter-free number formatting.

items.name: chat-thread
items.title: Chat Thread
items.description: Message thread that shows three bouncing typing dots before a "them" reply, pops bubbles in, and scrolls up as it fills.
items.docs:
Usage:

<PhoneFrame>
  <ChatThread
    messages={[
      { from: "me", text: "Can it render 9:16?", at: 0 },
      { from: "them", text: "Yes — same component, three formats.", at: 30 },
    ]}
  />
</PhoneFrame>

use: A DM, support chat or group thread inside a `phone-frame` or app mockup
Showing a bot or assistant "typing" before it answers
avoid: A single command-and-output log — use `terminal`

items.name: circle-burst
items.title: Circle Burst
items.description: A colored circle bursts out from a point to cover the frame, then a second circle opens from the same point onto the next scene.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <AppScreen />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition
    presentation={circleBurst({ origin: { x: 80, y: 20 } })}
    timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 30 })}
  />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <NextScreen />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Moving from a point of interest, like a button, logo or face, into the next scene
Bold, playful scene changes in social clips

items.name: code-block
items.title: Code Block
items.description: Themed editor card with syntax colors, line numbers and a file tab that can type code out, focus lines and mark a diff.

use: Showing an API, config file or snippet in a launch, docs or tutorial video
Typing code on screen, then focusing the lines that matter
avoid: Shell sessions with commands and output — use `terminal`

items.name: code-tokens
items.title: Code Tokens
items.description: Tiny dependency-free syntax tokenizer for ts, js, tsx, py, bash and json. Powers code-block and terminal.

items.name: command-palette
items.title: Command Palette
items.description: Search panel that types a query, narrows the list live, glides its highlight to the surviving match and presses it.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <CommandPalette
    items={[{ label: "New project" }, { label: "New template" }, { label: "Open settings" }]}
    query="new t"
    select="New template"
    selectAt={70}
  />
</Center>

use: A ⌘K launcher, quick switcher or fuzzy search in a product demo
Showing how fast a search or command feature narrows results
avoid: A shell session with commands and output — use `terminal`

items.name: comment-bubble
items.title: Comment Bubble
items.description: A viewer comment card, optionally marked as a reply, with a like count that ticks up.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <CommentBubble name="Katherine" handle="@kj" text="Which mic is that?" replyTo="Ada" likes={42} />
</Center>

use: Answering a comment on camera
Showing the question a video is about to answer
avoid: A full post with author metrics — use `post-card`

items.name: confetti
items.title: Confetti
items.description: Seeded confetti burst with closed-form physics: launch spread, gravity, air drag, spin and flutter, in theme colors.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence from={45} durationInFrames={90}>
  <Confetti origin={{ x: 50, y: 70 }} count={120} />
</Sequence>

use: Launches, milestones and end cards
Celebrating the moment a number or result lands
avoid: Emphasis on a single word or button — use `sparkle-burst`

items.name: core-math
items.title: Core Math
items.description: Pure, dependency-free math behind Core's motion and text helpers: motion quantization, stagger ordering, Catmull-Rom keyframe interpolation, the typing-reveal model, grapheme splitting and 0-1 clamping. No React, no DOM — safe to unit-test directly.
items.docs:
Usage:

const delay = staggerDelay(2, 5, { step: 4 }); // 8
const initial = graphemeInitial("👩‍🚀 Ada"); // "👩‍🚀"

items.name: core-physical-light
items.title: Core Physical Light
items.description: Shared "physical light" background looks for midnight/paper/neon/mono, reused by aurora, gradient-mesh, beams and spotlight. Not a catalog item on its own — each background item still owns its per-theme LOOK_BY_THEME mapping and its own default (curtains/blobs/shafts/pool) look for daylight/sunset.
items.docs:
Usage:

<GridSweepLook theme={theme} seconds={seconds} strength={0.6} background={theme.colors.background} />

items.name: core-stroke
items.title: Core Stroke
items.description: Pure stroke-width math behind theme.stroke's `brush` look, kept separate from core-math.ts so its one export stays easy to find and test on its own.
items.docs:
Usage:

const width = baseWidth * strokeWidthProfile(0.5, "arrow"); // thickest mid-stroke

items.name: core
items.title: Core
items.description: Theme tokens, responsive design units, platform safe zones and motion presets. Every reelcn component builds on this file.
items.docs:
Usage:

<ThemeProvider theme="midnight">
  <Stage>
    <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
  </Stage>
</ThemeProvider>

items.name: countdown
items.title: Countdown
items.description: A ring that empties while the number counts down to zero.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence durationInFrames={150}>
  <Countdown seconds={5} label="Starting in" />
</Sequence>

use: Waiting rooms and "starting soon" cards for streams
Timed challenges inside a video

items.name: counter
items.title: Counter
items.description: Number that counts between two values with Intl formatting, or rolls its digits like an odometer.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Counter to={48200} format={{ style: "currency", currency: "USD" }} suffix="/mo" rolling />
</Center>

use: Revenue, users, downloads and other headline metrics
Prices and percentages that should tick up on screen
avoid: A metric with a label and a change indicator — use `stat-counter`
Several metrics at once — use `kpi-grid`

items.name: cursor
items.title: Cursor
items.description: Pointer that glides between waypoints over whatever is behind it, pressing down and rippling on a click.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <BrowserWindow url="app.dev">
    <Dashboard />
  </BrowserWindow>
  <Cursor
    waypoints={[
      { x: 20, y: 30, frame: 0 },
      { x: 62, y: 48, frame: 30, click: true },
      { x: 62, y: 70, frame: 60 },
    ]}
  />
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Demonstrating a click path through a UI mockup, dashboard or website
Drawing the eye to a button just before a `toast` or `callout` appears
avoid: A static pointer aimed at one target — use `arrow`

items.name: data-story
items.title: Data Story
items.description: Report video that walks through numbers: a title, then one bar, line, donut or stat scene per section with its caption.

use: Quarterly results, year-in-review and research findings
Turning a dashboard into a narrated walkthrough
avoid: A single number — use `stat-counter`

items.name: dialog
items.title: Dialog
items.description: Modal that opens with an overlay fade and a 0.95→1 popup scale, capped by the safe zone so it never bleeds off-screen in portrait.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Dialog id="confirm" title="Delete staging-db-7?" steps={[{ at: 0, state: "closed" }, { at: 0.5, state: "open" }]} place={{ x: 50, y: 50 }}>
  <Button id="submit" label="Delete database" variant="primary" place={{ x: 50, y: 60 }} />
</Dialog>

use: A confirmation or form modal in a UI-sim walkthrough, composing `button`/`input` as its body
A `ui` scene's `component: "dialog"`
avoid: A modal with no real content — use `callout`

items.name: donut
items.title: Donut
items.description: Ring chart whose segments sweep in one after another around a counting total, with a legend beside it (below in portrait and square).
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Donut
    label="Visits"
    data={[
      { label: "Search", value: 4200 },
      { label: "Direct", value: 2600 },
      { label: "Social", value: 1500 },
      { label: "Email", value: 700 },
    ]}
  />
</Center>

use: Share of a whole: traffic sources, budget split, time spent across a few groups
Two to six segments
avoid: A single percentage — use `progress-ring`
Many small categories — use `bar-chart`

items.name: dots
items.title: Dots
items.description: Dot matrix with a soft wave of brighter, larger dots sweeping or rippling across it.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <Dots wave="ripple" />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

use: Clean tech, SaaS and data scenes that want texture without lines
Behind charts, code blocks and UI mockups
avoid: A structured line pattern or a perspective floor — use `grid`

items.name: drop-in
items.title: Drop In
items.description: Headline whose words drop in from above with a slight tilt that settles.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <DropIn text="Fresh drops every Friday" />
</Center>

use: Playful announcements, drops and release titles
Friendly, casual brands
avoid: Serious or premium tone — use `blur-in`

items.name: end-screen
items.title: End Screen
items.description: Closing screen with a next-video slot, a subscribe slot and a countdown.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Sequence from={900} durationInFrames={240}>
  <EndScreen title="Watch this next" nextTitle="How we cut render times in half" seconds={8} />
</Sequence>

use: The last ten seconds of a long-form video
Handing viewers one clear next step

items.name: feature-card
items.title: Feature Card
items.description: Icon, title, body copy and an optional badge on a themed card that rises into place.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <FeatureCard title="Zero config" body="Install with shadcn, no path aliases." badge="New" />
</Center>

A pricing tier or plan card with a "New" or "Popular" badge
avoid: Several feature tiles on one canvas at once — use `bento-grid`

items.name: feature-short
items.title: Feature Short
items.description: Vertical short about one feature: a hook, the feature in a line, the feature running on a phone, and a call to action.

use: Social shorts that show off a single feature
Weekly "did you know" clips for a product
avoid: A full product story — use `product-launch`

items.name: fit-title
items.title: Fit Title
items.description: One-line title that sizes itself to fill the available width, measured with the real font once it has loaded.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <FitTitle text="Season finale" effect="mask" />
</Center>

use: Big one-word or short titles that should fill the frame at every aspect ratio
Titles of unknown length, such as data-driven names or chapter titles
avoid: Headlines that should wrap onto several lines — use `text-reveal`

items.name: flash
items.title: Flash
items.description: Full-frame flash with a near-instant attack and an exponential decay, fired at `delay`.

Usage:

<Flash delay={24} strength={0.8} />

Camera-flash moments and reveals
avoid: A slow, warm glow over footage — use `light-leak`

items.name: follow-card
items.title: Follow Card
items.description: A profile card whose follow button presses itself and flips to "Following", with the count ticking up.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <FollowCard name="Ada Lovelace" handle="@ada" followers="24.8k" />
</Center>

use: Asking for a follow at the end of a short
Introducing a guest or a collaborator
avoid: A subscribe ask for long-form video — use `subscribe-cta`

items.name: fonts
items.title: Fonts
items.description: Loads the curated font set used by the built-in themes, so renders look identical on every machine.

items.name: glitch
items.title: Glitch
items.description: A digital hit: RGB channel split and seeded horizontal slice offsets build to a peak, cut to the next scene, then settle.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={45}>
    <Hook />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={glitch({ intensity: 1.2 })} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 16 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <Reveal />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Tech, gaming and music edits
Hard cuts that need a jolt of energy
avoid: Calm, premium or corporate pieces — use `card-push`

items.name: gradient-mesh

</AbsoluteFill>

use: Hero scenes, launch titles and product intros that need color and gentle motion
Behind glass cards, device frames and stat callouts

items.name: grain
items.title: Grain
items.description: Animated film-grain overlay from SVG noise that re-seeds every few frames; place it last, over anything.
items.docs:

  <GradientMesh />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>

</AbsoluteFill>

Breaking up banding in dark gradients such as `gradient-mesh` or `aurora`

items.name: grid
items.title: Grid
items.description: Line grid that pans slowly, or a perspective floor that scrolls toward the viewer and fades into a glowing horizon.
items.docs:
Usage:

<AbsoluteFill>
  <Grid perspective />
  <Center><TextReveal text="Hello" /></Center>
</AbsoluteFill>

Retro or futuristic openers with the perspective floor
avoid: A soft dotted texture — use `dots`

items.name: highlight
items.title: Highlight
items.description: Sentence with one phrase emphasized by a marker sweep, a hand-drawn underline or circle, or an outlined box.
items.docs:

<Center>
  <Highlight text="Render videos with plain React" highlight="plain React" variant="marker" />
</Center>

Tutorial titles that point at a single term
avoid: Cycling through several words in one slot — use `word-rotator`

</Sequence>

Restating the promise over b-roll halfway through
avoid: Full headlines in landscape video — use `text-reveal`

items.name: input

use: A sign-up or checkout field a cursor clicks into and types
A `ui` scene's `component: "input"`
avoid: A field that never receives focus — use plain text

items.name: kpi-grid

items.description: Two to six stat cards that pop in one after another, reflowing to up to four columns in landscape (never leaving a lone card on its own row), two in square, and one or two in portrait.

<Center>
  <KpiGrid
    items={[
      { label: "MRR", to: 48200, format: { style: "currency", currency: "USD", maximumFractionDigits: 0 }, delta: 12.4 },

      { label: "Churn", to: 2.1, suffix: "%", delta: -0.4 },
      { label: "NPS", to: 61, delta: 4 },

use: A dashboard summary slide: revenue, users, churn and NPS side by side
End-of-video recap of the numbers that mattered
avoid: A single metric — use `stat-counter`

items.name: laptop-frame
items.title: Laptop Frame
items.description: Laptop lid with a bezel around your screen content, sitting on a simple deck with a hinge line.

Two builds side by side inside `split-screen` for a before/after

    <After />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

Hiding the jump between two very different scenes

Manifesto-style sequences and closing statements

Splitting a blog post into a quick video

Naming a speaker, product or location on screen

Section titles and short-form hooks

Mixing reelcn transitions with the ones built into @remotion/transitions

<Center>

Editorial or retro looks that want a mechanical rhythm

Showing who is speaking when there is no camera

items.name: svg-draw
items.title: Svg Draw
items.description: Draws any set of SVG paths on stroke by stroke, staggered, with an optional fill fade once each finishes.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <SvgDraw viewBox="0 0 24 24" paths={["M4 12h16", "M4 6h10", "M4 18h7"]} size={220} />
</Center>

use: A logo mark, icon or custom illustration drawing itself on screen
Sketching a diagram or shape that a `callout` or label then points at
avoid: A single hand-drawn circle or arrow — use `scribble-circle` or `arrow`

items.name: switch
items.title: Switch
items.description: Toggle that flips between off and on with one physical move: the thumb's travel, on the theme's bouncy motion, nothing else animates.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Switch id="notifications" label="Push notifications" steps={[{ at: 0, state: "off" }, { at: 1, state: "on" }]} />
</Center>

use: A settings row in a UI-sim walkthrough
A `ui` scene's `component: "switch"`
avoid: A single static state with no flip — use plain text or an icon

items.name: tabs
items.title: Tabs
items.description: Tab row where one continuous fractional index positions the sliding pill, the lit label color and a small per-row parallax — nothing animates independently of that one number.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Tabs id="view" labels={["Overview", "Usage", "Billing"]} steps={[{ at: 0, state: { active: 0 } }, { at: 1, state: { active: 2 } }]} />
</Center>

use: Switching between views inside a UI-sim walkthrough
A `ui` scene's `component: "tabs"`
avoid: Two or fewer static labels with no switch — use plain text

items.name: talking-head-short
items.title: Talking Head Short
items.description: Vertical talking-head clip with a three-second hook and word-by-word captions, running as long as the video.

use: Turning a recorded explanation or interview answer into a short
Captioned clips for feeds that autoplay muted
avoid: Captions over a layout you build yourself — use `captions`

items.name: terminal
items.title: Terminal
items.description: Terminal window that types commands, prints their output line by line and scrolls as it fills.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Terminal
    lines={[
      { type: "command", text: "npx shadcn@latest add ./r/terminal.json" },
      { type: "output", text: "Created 3 files" },
    ]}
  />
</Center>

use: Install steps, CLI demos and deploy logs in product and tutorial videos
Any sequence of shell commands with their output
avoid: Source files or snippets without a prompt — use `code-block`

items.name: testimonial-reel
items.title: Testimonial Reel
items.description: Square reel of customer quotes, one card per testimonial, pushed in one after another.

use: Social proof for a landing page or an ad
Collecting launch-day reactions into one clip
avoid: One quote on its own — use `quote-card`

items.name: text-mask-video
items.title: Text Mask Video
items.description: Type acts as a window onto footage: the glyphs are the only place the video or image beneath shows through.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TextMaskVideo text="MOTION" src={staticFile("b-roll.mp4")} />

use: A headline that IS the footage, not a caption on top of it
Brand reveals where the type and the shot are the same idea

items.name: text-morph
items.title: Text Morph
items.description: Morphs one phrase into another: shared letters fly to their new position, leftover letters blur in or out instead of a plain cross-fade.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <TextMorph from="Build faster" to="Ship faster" />
</Center>

use: Before/after headlines, "problem → solution" hooks
A single word swap that should feel connected, not like two separate reveals

items.name: text-reveal
items.title: Text Reveal
items.description: Headline that animates in by word, character or line with rise, blur, fade, scale, drop or mask effects.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <TextReveal text="Ship videos, not keyframes" effect="blur" accentWords={["videos"]} />
</Center>

use: Hero headlines, section titles and short-form hooks
Any line of up to about twelve words that needs an entrance

items.name: tile-reveal
items.title: Tile Reveal
items.description: A grid of tiles pops in over the outgoing scene in a diagonal or seeded wave, then clears the same way onto the next scene.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <Gallery />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={tileReveal({ pattern: "random" })} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 36 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <Project />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Openers and section breaks with a designed, grid-based feel
Moving between portfolio, gallery or dashboard scenes

items.name: timeline
items.title: Timeline
items.description: Milestones on a single axis whose line draws on while dots pop and labels rise in sequence; horizontal in landscape and square, vertical in portrait.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Timeline
    milestones={[
      { label: "Founded", date: "2019", body: "Two co-founders, one laptop" },
      { label: "Seed round", date: "2021", body: "$3.2M raised" },
      { label: "Series A", date: "2023", body: "40 people, 12 countries" },
      { label: "1M events/day", date: "2025" },
    ]}
  />
</Center>

use: A roadmap, launch history or step-by-step process with three to seven beats
Company milestones or a project's key dates
avoid: Ranked values changing over time — use `bar-race`

items.name: toast-stack
items.title: Toast Stack
items.description: Several toasts, staggered in time, that close up smoothly as each one leaves — a running sum of occupancy-weighted heights, no measured DOM.
items.docs:
Usage:

<ToastStack
  toasts={[
    { at: 0, toast: { variant: "success", title: "Deployed", description: "Live in 12 regions" } },
    { at: 1.2, toast: { variant: "info", title: "Cache warmed" } },
    { at: 2.4, toast: { variant: "success", title: "Health check passed" } },
  ]}
/>

use: Several sequential confirmations or status updates in one product demo
Simulating a busy notification tray without hand-placing each card
avoid: A single notification — use `toast`

items.name: toast
items.title: Toast
items.description: Notification card with a status icon that slides in from an edge, holds, then slides back out.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Toast variant="success" title="Deployed" description="Live in 12 regions" />

use: Confirming an action, a deploy, an upload or a saved state in a product demo
A short system message that appears over a UI mockup
avoid: A message pointing at part of the screen — use `callout`

items.name: tutorial
items.title: Tutorial
items.description: Step-by-step coding tutorial: typed code, terminal sessions and screenshots, one step per scene, timed to the typing.

use: Getting-started guides and "how to" videos for developer tools
Walking through a setup one command at a time
avoid: A single snippet — use `code-block`

items.name: typewriter
items.title: Typewriter
items.description: Types text out character by character, with pause markers and a caret that blinks once typing stops.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Typewriter text="Make a launch video^ for vertical" cps={20} />
</Center>

use: Prompts, search queries and chat-style reveals
Quotes and statements that should read at speaking pace
avoid: Code listings — use `code-block`
Shell commands with output — use `terminal`

items.name: use-beat
items.title: Use Beat
items.description: A pulse that follows a fixed tempo, with no audio analysis: pure math, so it renders identically every time.

use: Cutting, popping or shaking anything in time with a music bed
Beat-synced motion when you know the track's BPM
avoid: Reacting to a voice or an unknown track — use `audio-reactive`

items.name: versus
items.title: Versus
items.description: Two-column comparison: numbers become mirrored bars, booleans become check/cross marks, strings stay text, and the side with more wins is highlighted in the accent.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <Versus
    left="Starter"
    right="Pro"
    rows={[
      { label: "Price / mo", left: 19, right: 49 },
      { label: "Seats included", left: 5, right: 25 },
      { label: "Priority support", left: false, right: true },
      { label: "Response time", left: "48h", right: "2h" },
    ]}
  />
</Center>

use: Plan or tier comparisons, before/after specs, us-vs-them feature tables
Three to eight rows mixing numbers, yes/no features and short text
avoid: A single trend over time — use `line-chart`

items.name: waveform
items.title: Waveform
items.description: The audio's shape, drawn as bars, a line or a mirrored band that moves with the sound.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Waveform src={staticFile("episode.mp3")} variant="mirror" bars={64} />

use: Audiograms and podcast clips
Any full-bleed band of motion tied to a voice or a track
avoid: A frequency view — use `spectrum`

items.name: whip-pan
items.title: Whip Pan
items.description: A fast directional blur hides a hard cut between two scenes, like a camera whipped from one framing to the next.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <SceneA />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={whipPan({ axis: "x" })} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 18 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <SceneB />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Fast-paced cuts between shots, especially ones that already move the same direction
Sports, action and hype-reel scene changes

items.name: word-push
items.title: Word Push
items.description: Words accelerate in one after another, each adding a small cumulative zoom so the whole line reads as one continuous push.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <WordPush words={["Ship", "videos,", "not", "keyframes"]} />
</Center>

use: Hook lines and headline builds on Shorts/Reels-style content
Any word-by-word reveal that should speed up, not stay evenly paced

items.name: word-rotator
items.title: Word Rotator
items.description: Sentence with one slot that cycles through a list of words by sliding, flipping or blurring them in place.
items.docs:
Usage:

<Center>
  <WordRotator before="Made for" words={["creators", "startups", "agencies"]} effect="slide" />
</Center>

use: Taglines that list audiences, platforms or benefits
Hooks such as "Made for creators / startups / agencies"
avoid: Emphasizing one fixed phrase — use `highlight`

items.name: youtube-intro
items.title: YouTube Intro
items.description: Channel opener: the channel mark, then the video's title, joined by an accent sweep.

use: The first seconds of a YouTube video or a series episode
avoid: End cards — use `youtube-outro`

items.name: youtube-outro
items.title: YouTube Outro
items.description: Ten-second end card with a next-video slot and a subscribe slot, sized for YouTube's end-screen elements.

use: The last seconds of a YouTube video
avoid: Openers — use `youtube-intro`

items.name: zoom-through
items.title: Zoom Through
items.description: Pushes through the outgoing scene and pulls back out of the incoming one, like the camera flew through the cut.
items.docs:
Usage:

<TransitionSeries>
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <FeatureOne />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
  <TransitionSeries.Transition presentation={zoomThrough()} timing={linearTiming({ durationInFrames: 24 })} />
  <TransitionSeries.Sequence durationInFrames={60}>
    <FeatureTwo />
  </TransitionSeries.Sequence>
</TransitionSeries>

use: Feature-to-feature walkthroughs and product demo cuts
Any transition that should feel like forward momentum, not a flat cut

items.name: check-determinism
items.title: Check Determinism
items.description: Scans your source for code that renders differently each time: wall-clock time, unseeded randomness, CSS animation and direct canvas-size reads.
items.docs:
Usage:

node scripts/reelcn-check-determinism.ts
node scripts/reelcn-check-determinism.ts src remotion

use: Before a final render, or as a CI step

items.name: contact-sheet
items.title: Contact Sheet
items.description: Renders one PNG grid of evenly spaced frames from any composition, so a whole video can be reviewed in a single image.
items.docs:
Usage:

node scripts/reelcn-contact-sheet.ts ProductLaunch
node scripts/reelcn-contact-sheet.ts Storyboard --frames 9 --props story.json --out review.png
node scripts/reelcn-contact-sheet.ts MyVideo --entry src/index.ts

items.name: sfx-pull
items.title: SFX Pull
items.description: Downloads the reelcn sound pack into your public folder so renders work offline.
items.docs:
Usage:

node scripts/reelcn-sfx-pull.ts

use: Rendering on a machine with no network, or in CI
Pinning the sounds so a later reelcn release cannot change them

items.name: transcribe
items.title: Transcribe
items.description: Turns audio or video into word-level captions JSON for the caption components.
items.docs:
Usage:

node scripts/reelcn-transcribe.ts talk.mp4
node scripts/reelcn-transcribe.ts talk.mp4 --openai --out public/captions/talk.json
node scripts/reelcn-transcribe.ts subtitles.srt

use: Captioning a talking-head short, a podcast clip or a tutorial
Converting an existing .srt into the caption format
